security_audit.summary: Most external command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline backticks. The confirmed issues are limited to documented npx install commands and one remote image, which create supply-chain or passive network exposure if used without review. No evidence of prompt injection, credential access, or data exfiltration was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Pin package versions, document the source for widgets.json, provide a checksum or commit reference, and require confirmation before running the command.
Mark related skill installation as optional and require explicit approval before running npx skills add commands from the documentation.
Use a marketplace-hosted image or proxy the remote asset to avoid passive requests to an external domain during documentation rendering.

content.value_statement: Teams need a consistent way to render rich UI from structured agent output. This skill shows how to use widgets-ui with React, Next.js, shadcn, forms, actions, and display components.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to install the widgets-ui registry with shadcn.
Shows how to render a WidgetRenderer component in React or Next.js.
Documents layout, typography, interactive, and display widget types.
Provides examples for flight cards, contact forms, and action handling.
Lists supported gradient names for box backgrounds.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not include the renderer source code.
It depends on external ui.inference.sh and inference.sh resources.
It does not validate generated widget data for safety or completeness.
It does not describe accessibility, authentication, or backend persistence.

use_cases.title: Prototype Agent Interfaces
use_cases.description: Create quick React widget layouts from structured agent responses for demos and internal tools.

use_cases.title: Render Dynamic Forms
use_cases.description: Define inputs, selects, text areas, checkboxes, and submit actions from widget schemas.

use_cases.title: Standardize UI Output
use_cases.description: Give agents a repeatable widget vocabulary for cards, badges, icons, images, and layout blocks.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Basic Widget
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a simple card or form.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a widgets-ui component plan for a simple contact card. Include the visible fields, actions, and layout choices.

prompt_templates.title: Design A Form Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate form generation for user input.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a widgets-ui form for collecting support requests. Include required fields, select options, checkbox text, and submit behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Agent Output
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced transformation from structured response to UI.
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this structured agent response into a widgets-ui layout. Explain which widget types map to each section and why.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Production Integration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced implementation planning for a React app.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review a proposed widgets-ui integration for a Next.js app. Cover action handling, validation, error states, and external dependency risks.

output_examples.input: Create a flight status card for departure and arrival information.
output_examples.output: A compact card plan with two columns, airport titles, a center travel icon, captions, and an ocean gradient background.

output_examples.input: Create a contact form that submits name, email, and message.
output_examples.output: A vertical form plan with labeled fields, a message area, a send button, and submit action guidance.

output_examples.input: Explain how to handle widget button actions in React.
output_examples.output: A handler plan that separates submit and click actions, passes form data, and records expected UI behavior.

best_practices: Review generated widget data before rendering it in a production application.
Require user confirmation before running installation commands from the skill.
Keep widget actions explicit, typed, and limited to expected form or click events.
anti_patterns: Do not render untrusted widget data without validation and content limits.
Do not run remote installer commands automatically from an agent response.
Do not treat widget examples as a complete accessibility or security model.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build React and Next.js interfaces from structured widget descriptions.

faq.question: Does it include backend code?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on frontend widget rendering, examples, and action handling patterns.

faq.question: Can agents use it to create forms?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents inputs, text areas, selects, checkboxes, buttons, and submit actions.

faq.question: Does it require external resources?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented installer and reference links use ui.inference.sh and inference.sh resources.

faq.question: Is generated widget data automatically safe?
faq.answer: No. Applications should validate widget data before rendering or acting on it.

faq.question: Which AI tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
